Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid an alleged Chinese espionage scandal, and the high-stakes Anthropic IPO landing in its shadow. Outlets are also tracking a sharp AI-stocks selloff, a global Microsoft/FAA tech outage, and US-China tensions ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.

stories.headline: Nvidia leadership crisis deepens with Bessent, Congress and Musk weighing in
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is pushing Nvidia to install an outside CEO and has questioned whether the chipmaker skirted China export restrictions, while Congress moves to tighten AI chip export rules and Commerce Secretary Lutnick faces mounting scrutiny over his ties to the company; Elon Musk has meanwhile called for Jensen Huang's reinstatement.

stories.headline: Anthropic's historic IPO lands as a referendum on the AI trade
stories.summary: Anthropic is set to debut on the Nasdaq this week in what could be the largest IPO ever, with Nvidia, Google and other partners committing $26 billion in a concurrent private placement; the listing comes just days after Nvidia's first earnings report without Jensen Huang, making it a high-stakes test of investor faith in AI according to multiple outlets.

stories.headline: Data center construction stocks lose $4.2 trillion as AI trade unravels
stories.summary: Shares in AI 'picks and shovels' companies have been hit hard by a broader tech sell-off, as instability at Nvidia and questions over the AI buildout spook markets, with the Nasdaq erasing nearly $2.5 trillion in a single session according to Fortune's reporting.

stories.headline: Microsoft Outlook outage and FAA groundstop expose tech fragility
stories.summary: A global Microsoft Outlook/Teams/Copilot outage that disrupted government services, hospitals and police departments, coinciding with an FAA router failure, has highlighted how dependent critical infrastructure is on a handful of fragile tech systems; Microsoft says services are now fully restored.

stories.headline: US and allies sign accord to shield AI supply chains from China ahead of Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: The United States and allied nations have signed a pact aimed at protecting AI supply chains from China, timed just ahead of President Trump's planned meeting with Xi Jinping at the APEC forum in Shenzhen.

stories.headline: SpaceX achieves historic Starship rocket catch
stories.summary: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned from orbit and was caught at the same Texas launch site, a milestone toward the company's vision of fully reusable rockets.

stories.headline: Megaspeed discloses timeline of Alice Huang's departure, deepening Nvidia spy scandal
stories.summary: Singapore-based Megaspeed disclosed that former executive Alice Huang, who had a relationship with ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and is suspected by US officials of spying for China, left the company in August 2025, adding new detail to the unfolding timeline.

stories.headline: Nvidia scandal reaches the heart of Trump's cabinet
stories.summary: The fallout from Jensen Huang's downfall is spreading into the Trump administration, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick facing pointed questions over his handling of chip export policy toward China.

Business.gaps: Puck, Forbes and Business Insider yielded little distinct business coverage beyond general Jensen Huang/Nvidia commentary already found via Fortune and Axios; Politico's recent items were largely political (midterms, MAGA polling) rather than business-focused so were excluded.

US politics.overview: US politics coverage is dominated by the fallout from Democrats' sweeping midterm wins, including a rare internal leadership fight as Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, and a Friday nationwide FAA ground stop that has triggered a scramble for billions in emergency air-traffic-control funding. Outlets are also tracking Democrats' post-election strategy sessions in Denver, a brewing Nvidia/China national-security scandal threatening Commerce Secretary Lutnick, and escalating Iran-related tensions testing the Trump-Vance relationship.

stories.headline: Van Hollen challenges Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is mounting an insurgent bid against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader ahead of a Dec. 1 secret-ballot vote, with Van Hollen claiming over 10 senators' support while Schumer says he has the votes to win, exposing deep divisions in the party just after its historic midterm sweep.

stories.headline: Trump administration escalates funding demands after nationwide FAA ground stop
stories.summary: After Friday's nationwide ground stop, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy raised his ask to Congress to $50 billion for air-traffic-control modernization, up from $30.1 billion a day earlier, while Democrats including Van Hollen question why previously appropriated funds weren't fully spent.

stories.headline: Democrats gather in Denver to chart post-midterm path, warn against overreach
stories.summary: Democrats from across the country met in Denver for a two-day conference following their sweeping midterm victories, with party figures warning the sweeping wins could be squandered if the party doesn't manage its newfound power carefully.

stories.headline: Nvidia/China scandal puts Commerce Secretary Lutnick in the crosshairs
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has reportedly blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department for inaction as questions mount over senior Trump officials' knowledge of an alleged Chinese spy's ties to Nvidia's Jensen Huang, with Lutnick facing calls for his ouster.

stories.headline: Supreme Court agrees to hear case on Trump's asylum suspension
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has agreed to take up a challenge to the Trump administration's suspension of asylum processing, setting up a major ruling on executive authority over immigration law.

stories.headline: Vance and Trump diverge on how to end the Iran War as Bahrain fends off Iranian drone strikes
stories.summary: A rift is opening between President Trump and Vice President Vance over how to end the Iran War, even as Bahrain said it intercepted a six-drone Iranian attack on a U.S. airbase early Sunday.

stories.headline: Pentagon prepares own prosecution of general accused of leaking
stories.summary: Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia now faces legal jeopardy on two fronts after the Pentagon moved to pursue its own prosecution following allegations from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's team that were already referred to the Justice Department.

stories.headline: Alaska elects first Democratic governor in two decades
stories.summary: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins flipped Alaska's governorship, marking the first time Alaskans have elected a Democrat to the corner office in more than two decades.

US politics.gaps: Punchbowl News and NOTUS had no recent (last 48-hour) coverage available via search; Cook Political Report's most recent available analysis predates the last 48 hours. Politico, NYT, WSJ, and The Guardian were limited to the feed items provided since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across nearly every tech and AI outlet is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid a Chinese espionage scandal, and by Anthropic's blockbuster, oversubscribed IPO expected to be the largest in history. Secondary threads include US-China tech decoupling (a new Pax Silica allied tech-protection pact, scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Lutnick, and reports Chinese labs are training on banned Nvidia chips), plus Apple's smart glasses plans and a nationwide FAA ground stop that renewed worries about tech fragility.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns, Creating Uncertainty for the AI Sector
stories.summary: The Information reports Jensen Huang's resignation 'upends the world's second-most-valuable company and rattles one of the foundations of the AI economy,' with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO; a staff and tech-industry petition (signed by Elon Musk and others) to reinstate him has drawn more than 100,000 signatures. VentureBeat separately assesses whether the departure could puncture the broader 'AI bubble,' noting Nvidia's extensive circular financing deals with AI startups as the biggest risk.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO Makes Dario Amodei the New Face of the AI Boom
stories.summary: Anthropic is set to go public this week in what is expected to be the largest IPO ever, with Bloomberg noting the debut will force Dario Amodei to fill the 'leading pitchman' void left by Huang while proving AI firms can turn infrastructure spending into real profit. The Decoder reports the offering, aiming to raise up to $64.4 billion at a roughly $1.4 trillion valuation, is already about six times oversubscribed even as Amodei admits 'huge uncertainty' over nearly $901 billion in compute commitments.

stories.headline: Bessent Urges Nvidia to Pick Outsider as Next CEO
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is pushing Nvidia to hire an external CEO and has demanded answers within 10 days on whether the company pushed 'seemingly illicit' chip sales to China to boost revenue. FT and Techmeme report the same demand for a leadership 'shake-up,' while the Economist and Guardian note the scandal is also fueling momentum in Congress for tighter chip export rules.

stories.headline: US and Pax Silica Allies Agree to Joint List of AI Technologies to Protect from China
stories.summary: The US and allies including Japan, the UK and India have agreed to create a joint list of AI technologies and supply chains to shield from China, timed ahead of Trump's meeting with Xi Jinping at the APEC forum in Shenzhen.

stories.headline: Investigation: Lutnick Pushed to Narrow Chip Curbs Affecting Former Firm's Client
stories.summary: An NYT investigation reported via Techmeme alleges Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick pushed to narrow chip export curbs affecting a client of his former firm, Cantor Fitzgerald, whose Malaysia data center may serve China's Tencent, adding to scrutiny as Lutnick is set to join Trump on a trip to China this week.

stories.headline: Chinese AI Labs Are Training Models on Nvidia's Blackwell Despite Export Controls
stories.summary: A forensic report cited by The Register finds fingerprints of Nvidia's export-banned Blackwell GPUs in models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group. TechCrunch similarly reports that China's most powerful open-weight AI models were trained on Nvidia chips the U.S. government had restricted from export, intensifying scrutiny of Nvidia amid the Huang scandal.

stories.headline: FAA Ground Stop and Microsoft Outlook Outage Expose Fragile Tech Dependence
stories.summary: NYT argues that back-to-back incidents involving Microsoft Outlook and a nationwide FAA ground stop this past week show how dependent daily life has become on fragile technology. Ars Technica and The Register report the FAA's third-ever nationwide ground stop was blamed on faulty, outdated equipment, while the FAA has separately been expanding an AI advisory tool across US airspace without involving the air traffic controllers' union.

stories.headline: Apple's First Smart Glasses Are Coming Together
stories.summary: The Verge reports Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says Apple's first smart glasses, which will lack augmented-reality features, are expected to be unveiled soon, with Techmeme detailing plans to show them at WWDC and ship by end of 2027 with deep Siri and third-party app integration.

Tech & AI.gaps: MIT Technology Review, Platformer, IEEE Spectrum, and Rest of World did not return any recent, group-relevant coverage in search; The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, and The Guardian were assessed only via the provided feed items since they block web search. Google DeepMind's own announcement channels did not surface any new company posts in the search results obtained.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, where a global electrification pledge and a steep drop in climate-finance commitments are the central storylines, alongside fresh data showing global fossil-fuel emissions may dip slightly in 2026 due to the Iran conflict. US-focused outlets are heavily tracking how the Trump administration's deregulatory and protectionist energy policies (grid equipment import bans, coal-plant support) are colliding with surging AI/data-center power demand and grid capacity constraints.

stories.headline: COP31's electrification pledge wins support, with caveats on clean power and finance
stories.summary: More than 50 countries are backing a pledge to raise electricity's share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035 from roughly 23% today, with the EU widely expected to join, while Greta Thunberg told the summit the planet 'is being killed.'

stories.headline: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
stories.summary: Carbon Brief analysis finds public climate-finance pledges to developing nations have collapsed to just $11.7bn a year from around $40bn, as the US has withdrawn from international climate efforts and European aid budgets shrink.

stories.headline: Fossil-fuel CO2 emissions set to dip in 2026 as Iran conflict hits oil use
stories.summary: New Global Carbon Project figures project a roughly 0.4% fall in fossil CO2 emissions for 2026, driven mainly by a 1.9% drop in oil emissions tied to higher prices and supply disruption from the Hormuz closure, though coal emissions continue to rise slightly.

stories.headline: Utility, tech officials see opportunities to increase grid utilization
stories.summary: At BNEF's Houston Summit, utility and tech panelists including Google's Tyler Norris said US grid utilization sits at just 40-60%, and that flexible interconnection deals with large data-center loads could free up significant capacity without new infrastructure.

stories.headline: Trump ban on foreign grid components sparks industry concern over cost, practicality
stories.summary: Industry stakeholders warned that Executive Order 14421, which lets Energy Secretary Chris Wright block foreign-made bulk-power equipment, could worsen existing shortages of transformers and substations even as it aims to address genuine security risks.

stories.headline: Consider the Lobstermen Affected by New York's Empire Wind
stories.summary: A family of lobstermen sued Equinor in federal court claiming the Empire Wind project's compensatory mitigation program failed to offset damage to lobster fishing grounds, a closely-watched case given the Trump administration's ongoing review of other offshore wind permits.

Energy.gaps: Could not find stories from the last 24-48 hours for Argus Media, Latitude Media, or E&E News; search results for these outlets mostly surfaced older articles (Latitude Media's most relevant piece was from Nov. 4, Argus Media's from May, and E&E News's from recent months but not this week). Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT, and The Economist block search, so only the energy-related feed items provided for those outlets could be considered, and none were on-topic for this group.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by two intertwined storylines: the run-up to the APEC Economic Leaders' summit in Shenzhen, where Trump, Xi and Putin are set for an unprecedented trilateral meeting, and the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO amid a Chinese espionage scandal. State-run outlets are promoting Shenzhen's summit preparations as a showcase of China's global economic leadership, while business and tech outlets dig into Nvidia's succession crisis and its ties to a Singapore-based chip buyer now linked to Chinese intelligence.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first-ever trilateral meeting at APEC Shenzhen summit
stories.summary: The White House said Trump will raise nuclear arms reduction when he meets Xi and Putin on the sidelines of the APEC forum in Shenzhen this week, a meeting China has resisted framing around weapons issues since it is hosting a summit meant to focus on trade. State-run Xinhua, Global Times and CGTN are promoting the November 18-19 summit as a showcase of China's role as a stabilizing economic power, while Hong Kong Free Press and Taipei Times flagged the historic three-way format.

stories.headline: Bessent presses Nvidia to pick an outsider as new CEO after Jensen Huang's ouster
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia needs to look outside the company for a new chief executive and questioned whether the chipmaker pushed illicit China sales to boost revenue, days after Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down. Caixin Global reported Nvidia shares have fallen more than 20% over the past month as the board's independent investigation into Huang's conduct continues, with Congress seeking a closed-door briefing.

stories.headline: Alleged Chinese spy tied to Nvidia scandal is now in Beijing, as Megaspeed dealings face scrutiny
stories.summary: Alice Huang, the Megaspeed International founder suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese agent, has returned to Beijing with the knowledge of security officials, Bloomberg reported. Caixin Global detailed how she built the Singapore data-center firm's reported assets from almost nothing to nearly $3 billion in three years while it became a major Nvidia chip buyer, and Beijing's foreign ministry has dismissed the spy allegations as a smear.

stories.headline: US and allies sign pact to shield AI supply chains from China ahead of Shenzhen summit
stories.summary: Washington and allied governments signed an agreement aimed at protecting AI supply chains from Chinese influence just ahead of Trump's trip to the APEC forum in Shenzhen, where he is due to meet Xi Jinping.

stories.headline: Congress moves to tighten AI chip export rules following Nvidia scandal
stories.summary: Lawmakers are advancing stricter rules on AI chip exports to China, with reporting suggesting Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset has added momentum to the push. ChinaTalk devoted an emergency podcast to the proposed MATCH Act in the wake of Huang's departure.

stories.headline: COMAC's CE-25A electric commercial aircraft completes first crewed flight
stories.summary: China's state-backed planemaker COMAC flew its 19-seat CE-25A electric aircraft with two pilots and a flight test engineer aboard, covering more than 60 kilometers in just over 16 minutes in its first crewed test.

stories.headline: Taiwan to extend Rednote restrictions and tighten cybersecurity after data breaches
stories.summary: Taiwanese officials are expected to extend restrictions on the Chinese app Rednote again, according to sources, as the foreign ministry separately rolled out tighter cybersecurity measures following recent data breaches affecting government-linked systems.

stories.headline: Nio opens its northernmost China battery-swap station to serve extreme-cold markets
stories.summary: Nio opened a new battery swap station in Heihe, Heilongjiang, its northernmost in China, touting 3-minute swaps even where temperatures can fall to -48°C, as the EV maker expands its charging network into harsh climates.

China.gaps: No recent China-specific coverage was found via search for Rest of World, Sixth Tone, China Media Project, The Wire China, Yicai Global or TechNode within the search allowance used; Reuters, AP, NYT and The Economist block search so only feed items (where provided) were used for them.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the widening regional war: Iran's renewed drone and missile attacks on Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, a Houthi advance that hands them control of the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint, and a senior Hamas commander's killing in Gaza. Israeli outlets are absorbed in the post-election scramble between Netanyahu and Eisenkot over forming a unity government, while business titles (AGBI, Arabian Business) are tracking the war's toll on Saudi markets, UAE industry and new Gulf investment deals with China.

stories.headline: Iran escalates attacks on Bahrain and Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched a drone strike on a US-linked radar site in Bahrain and the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and three drones over the Eastern Province, part of an intensifying low-level conflict. Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Jordan all condemned the Iranian strikes on Bahrain, which called on the UN Security Council to act.

stories.headline: Yemeni government forces retreat, handing Houthis control of Bab el-Mandeb Strait
stories.summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces withdrew from territory overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a retreat that analysts say hands Iran-aligned Houthi rebels greater leverage over one of the world's key maritime chokepoints for global shipping.

stories.headline: Senior Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
stories.summary: Hamas said a senior commander who had helped plan and oversee the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel was killed in an Israeli strike in southern Gaza, continuing Israel's pattern of targeting replacement commanders before they can rebuild Hamas's command structure.

stories.headline: Netanyahu and Eisenkot clash over Israeli unity government
stories.summary: Caretaker PM Benjamin Netanyahu renewed calls for a national unity government citing the Iran nuclear threat, while Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot, who holds the mandate to form a government, dismissed the offer as a "bluff" even as Likud and Yashar negotiating teams met to discuss a potential coalition.

stories.headline: Three oil tankers catch fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's navy said three oil tankers caught fire on Saturday after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state media, underscoring the continued danger to shipping through the critical oil corridor.

stories.headline: Jordan sentences three men to death over Karak church attack
stories.summary: A Jordanian court sentenced three men to death by hanging over a deadly shooting attack on a church in Karak, and the kingdom cancelled Christmas celebrations in solidarity with victims' families.

stories.headline: Saudi stocks rebound but war damage still weighs on Gulf industry
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's All-Shares Index closed the week 9 percent above its October five-year low but remained down 2 percent year-to-date, with recovery led by state-backed firms like Aramco-adjacent Acwa and Saudi National Bank even as Houthi missile threats keep pressuring profit margins. Separately, UAE-based Emirates Global Aluminium reported its debt rose 40 percent to $5 billion after an Iranian attack damaged its Al Taweelah smelter, cutting revenue 16 percent.

stories.headline: Oman signs multibillion-dollar investment package with China
stories.summary: Oman's sovereign wealth fund announced its largest-ever single-day package of investment agreements with Chinese institutions, including an $800 million joint fund with China's Silk Road Fund, highlighting growing Gulf competition to attract Chinese capital.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find recent (last 24-48h) region-relevant coverage from Khaleej Times, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Ynetnews or Iran International within the search allowance; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, The Economist and BBC block search so only WSJ feed items were available among that group.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across African outlets is dominated by security and governance stories playing out across the continent - from an Ebola scare at a major DRC mine and Sudan's deepening fuel crisis to diplomatic rifts at the Francophonie summit - alongside business stories on mining deals, African tech infrastructure and investment. Several business and mining outlets are also tracking a wave of corporate and financing news, including a major Angola-De Beers stake move and new foreign lending into Southern African projects.

stories.headline: Francophonie summit opens in Cambodia overshadowed by African tensions
stories.summary: DR Congo is threatening to quit the Francophonie organization if Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo is re-elected to a third term as its head, spilling Kinshasa-Kigali tensions onto the global stage.

stories.headline: Angola seeks 10% stake in De Beers under Anglo's proposed exit
stories.summary: Angola's mines ministry has told Reuters it wants a 10% holding in De Beers as part of Anglo American's planned sale of its stake in the diamond giant, a move that could reshape ownership of one of the world's top diamond producers.

stories.headline: Daily life in Sudan paralysed by deepening fuel crisis and rising costs
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war has crippled domestic oil refining while Middle East conflict volatility pushes prices higher, compounding hardship for ordinary Sudanese already battered by famine warnings.

stories.headline: South Sudan postpones first general election from December to February
stories.summary: South Sudan's electoral commission has delayed what would be the country's first-ever general election to February, citing the need for more time on voter registration materials and civic education.

stories.headline: Microsoft's outage showed Africa's banks had no real plan B
stories.summary: TechCabal's newsletter examines how a recent Microsoft cloud outage exposed the fragility of African banks' digital infrastructure and their lack of contingency planning.

stories.headline: David Moinina Sengeh: Sierra Leone is betting on West Africa
stories.summary: A profile piece looks at Sierra Leone's strategy to position itself within West African regional trade and investment networks as a path to growth.

stories.headline: Hassan Sheikh's enemies cut a deal
stories.summary: Africa Confidential reports that al-Shabaab is courting dissident clans in Somalia as President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's bid to extend his presidency strains the military campaign against the jihadist group.

Africa.gaps: The Continent yielded no stories from the last 48 hours in search (only older archived PDF issues were found). Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and no feed items for those outlets were provided for this beat, so their current coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Coverage across entertainment and media trades is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy, which outlets are also framing as a story about the power of investigative journalism. Entertainment trades are heavily focused on Billy Evans's first televised response to his portrayal in 'You Can See Everything,' Johnny Depp's box-office comeback with 'Ebenezer,' and SNL's topical cold open, while journalism-focused outlets are tracking AI's reshaping of the news business, from publisher lawsuits and licensing deals to AI-driven political ad spending and Washington Post's financial turnaround.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns After Multiple Affairs, Including With Alleged Chinese Spy
stories.summary: Nvidia's board forced out founder Jensen Huang after revelations of an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China and a second affair with a subordinate, a scandal that also hammered the company's stock over national security concerns. Mediaite and Puck both frame the saga as a case study in investigative journalism's power, with Congress now demanding to know what the White House knew about the relationship.

stories.headline: Billy Evans Defends Himself Against 'Controlling Monster' Portrayal in 'You Can See Everything'
stories.summary: In his first televised interview, Elizabeth Holmes's husband Billy Evans pushed back on his depiction in the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim A24 documentary and said he has no regrets about participating, while also telling Deadline he "did not give consent" for nudity included in the film.

stories.headline: Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Tops Box Office With $19 Million Domestic, $42 Million Worldwide
stories.summary: Depp's modest Christmas Carol redo took the No. 1 domestic spot with $19 million while performing stronger overseas, as Amazon MGM's heist film 'How to Rob a Bank' flopped with just $5 million.

stories.headline: 'SNL' Cold Open Skewers RFK Jr., Jensen Huang and FAA Travel Chaos
stories.summary: Host John Mulaney devoted much of his monologue to mocking HHS Secretary RFK Jr., while Bowen Yang returned as a disgraced Jensen Huang advising tech CEOs amid the real-life Nvidia scandal, in an episode that also referenced the weekend's nationwide FAA ground stop.

stories.headline: The Washington Post Nears Breakeven After 'Hundreds and Hundreds of Millions' in Losses
stories.summary: Adweek reports the Post is approaching financial breakeven following a prolonged period of heavy losses, a notable turnaround story for one of the industry's most closely watched legacy newsrooms.

stories.headline: News Publishers Escalate AI Litigation: NYT, Chicago Tribune and Others Sue Brave Software
stories.summary: Press Gazette's running tracker shows US newspapers including the New York Times suing browser maker Brave for allegedly scraping articles for AI firms, Canadian publishers suing Anthropic, and Reach and CNN signing new AI licensing deals with Google, amid a wave of similar suits and deals globally.

stories.headline: Political Campaigns Spent $187 Million Promoting AI-Generated Ads in the 2026 Midterms
stories.summary: Poynter found midterm campaigns spent $187 million boosting AI-generated ads, more than 3,000 times the spend in 2024, with roughly 90% of that spending coming from Republican-affiliated groups.

stories.headline: Russell Brand Accuser Waives Anonymity, Alleging Rape at Age 16
stories.summary: One of Russell Brand's accusers has given up her legal right to anonymity to speak publicly after the comedian was imprisoned for rape and sexual assault.

Media.gaps: NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block direct search access and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so their current coverage could not be independently verified beyond mentions in other outlets' reporting.
